source.title: Can Trump's 'economic D-day' force Iran to capitulate?
source.author: Andrew England in London, Najmeh Bozorgmehr in Tehran and Joseph Leahy in Beijing
source.role: Control text for the discrimination test. Same outlet, same event, same week as the Bessent op-ed — news desk rather than opinion page, so genre is the only variable that changes.
source.caveat: This is news analysis, not a straight wire report. Analysis carries more interpretation than a bare account of what happened, so this is a conservative control — a pure wire story would likely score lower still.
source.note: Source text held locally and not committed — FT terms prohibit redistribution. Only short spans quoted here, for criticism.

fact.claim: China imported $11bn of goods from Iran and exported $13.4bn in the Iranian financial year to March; UAE trade totalled $21bn; Turkey $13.5bn.
fact.verifyWith: Attributed in-text to Iranian government data. Cross-check against Iranian customs administration figures and IMF Direction of Trade Statistics.

fact.claim: Year-on-year inflation is 'soaring towards 90 per cent' and the rial is hitting record lows almost daily.
fact.verifyWith: Statistical Centre of Iran CPI; open-market rial quotes. Note the op-ed made a similar claim without any source; this piece states a figure.

fact.claim: Trump withdrew from the 2015 nuclear accord in May 2018, beginning the 'maximum pressure' campaign.
fact.verifyWith: Standard record. Load-bearing for the article's argument, since the whole piece turns on comparison with that campaign.

fact.claim: 'maximum pressure' failed to force concessions and fostered a more hardline stance in Tehran.
fact.verifyWith: IAEA enrichment records for the period; the claim is contestable and is asserted in the article's own voice rather than attributed.

fact.claim: The UAE suspended all trade and financial transactions with Iran last week.

persuasion.span: force the Islamic regime to cave to its demands and lift its chokehold over the Strait of Hormuz
persuasion.mechanism: Two metaphors in the paper's own voice — 'cave' and 'chokehold' — assign posture and aggression rather than describing the blockade in neutral terms.
persuasion.neutral: press Iran to accept US terms and reopen the Strait of Hormuz

persuasion.span: the pain being heaped on the nation of about 90mn people
persuasion.mechanism: Passive construction with no 'by' phrase. Pain is heaped, but the sanctions regime doing the heaping is absent from the sentence.
persuasion.neutral: the pain US sanctions and the war are imposing on a nation of about 90mn people

persuasion.mechanism: Severity asserted through an adjective rather than through the measures' scope or effect.

persuasion.span: the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary
persuasion.mechanism: Same superlative flagged in the op-ed. Here it sits inside quotation marks and is explicitly credited to Bessent, so the language belongs to the source, not the paper.
persuasion.neutral: No rewrite needed — the article is reporting the claim, not making it.

persuasion.mechanism: Casts sovereign trading decisions as misconduct requiring correction. Bessent's framing, quoted and attributed.
persuasion.neutral: No rewrite needed — quoted and credited.

persuasion.mechanism: Escalation framing, attributed to Iran's top security official and presented as his characterisation rather than the paper's.
persuasion.neutral: No rewrite needed — quoted and credited.

actionable.question: Did 'maximum pressure' actually fail, or did it achieve different aims than the ones being measured?
actionable.how: The article asserts failure in its own voice. Compare Iranian oil export volumes, enrichment levels, and proxy funding across 2018-2021 — the answer differs depending on which metric is treated as the goal.

actionable.question: Who is quoted, and who is not?
actionable.how: Named sources here include a former Israeli military intelligence analyst, a Chatham House fellow, an Iranian analyst, and Iran's central bank governor — critics and Iranian voices both present. No serving US official is quoted beyond Bessent's public remarks. Compare against the op-ed, which quotes no one.

actionable.question: Is the 90 per cent inflation figure official or estimated?
actionable.how: Iranian official statistics and independent estimates diverge substantially. Check which is being used.
